builds.name: Base 51 Def
builds.desc: Walhart can reach a respectable spread of 46/46/27/51/24. This defense is absurd and combined with either Giant Spoon+ or Wo Gun+, Walhart has one of the strongest ignis in the game. Walhart is severely underrated in my opinion.

builds.name: Lightning McWalhart
builds.desc:
This build is mainly for people aiming to +10 Walhart. The nature of Walharts weapon makes him comparable to Legendary Ephraim and Legendary Eirika, a lone horse. However, unlike the two, Walhardt does not have a method of dual phase doubling (Ephraim with his weapon effect, Eirika with her super high speed stat of 39). This build attempts to fix this by making Walhart as speedy as he can be. There are alot of flexible slots in this build, so you can play around with it alot.
Wolf Berg is a cornerstone of this build. With this build he benefits for every stat boost, the +4 speed goes a long way for securing doubles. Atk/Spd Solo 3 is the other cornerstone to this build. Combined with his weapon, Walhart gains 10 extra attack, and more importantly, 10 extra speed. At +10 this bumps him up to 41 speed when away from allies. Any other A slot for this build will make it less consistent, however if you don't have this Solo skill, you can make do with Fury 3.
For the most part, the C slot is flexible, however Even Spd Wave 3 (or Odd Spd Wave 3) is a strong option, giving him more self reliance, it also bumps him up to 47 speed. If you were to run a different C skill, Spd Smoke 3 is the next best thing due to how well it sets him up for enemy phase. If you intend to run him on horse emblem, use whatever horse emblem buff your team needs.
The best seal options are Speed +3 for the obvious speed boost, Darting Stance 3 to make him harder to kill on player phase; even for the fastest of units like Ishtar, Raven Ayra etc. Heavy Blade 3 is good if you use the harder hitting specials. Quick Riposte can also be a solid option, turning fights vs Wary Fighter armors back into speed checks.
The special on this build is can be based mainly on what you choose for the seal slot. If you use a simple Speed +3 seal or Darting Stance 3, you can use any two turn special to guarantee proc in when you double, being Glimmer or Moonbow (even Noontime if you want, his attack can reach high levels to make solid use of it). If you use Heavy Blade 3 however, you may want to use the longer cooldown specials, best options being Bonfire or Ignis for damage, Aether for sustain, or Galeforce for a more fun approach.
The B slot is truly the most flexible slot, most B slots can work for any build. Chill Def 3 is a great budget option that works completely fine, Chill Spd 3 can be good for securing doubles. Renewal 3 is great for longer fights in modes like Grand Conquest. Guard 3 raises his survivability greatly. The movement B slots like Lunge and Hit and Run can make Galeforce builds very interesting. Pass 3 can catch people offguard on arena and aether defense and make it harder for you to bait. Vantage 3 or Desperation 3 messing with attack order can come in clutch at lower hp.
+10 Walhart with Wolf Berg, Atk/Spd Solo, Spd Wave and Speed +3 = 50 speed in optimal conditions. +10 Walhart with Wolf Berg, Atk/Spd Solo, Spd Wave and Darting Stance = 53 speed on enemy phase.

builds.name: The Conqueror's Whetstone
builds.desc: A build that focuses on Walhart's massive Defense stat potential. Wolf Berg and both of the Fortress Def 3s in both the A and S slots further enhance Walhart's already impressive Defense of 36 to 49. This is not counting the in-combat boost from Wolf Berg when the number of foes around Walhart exceeds the number of allies around him- with this extra boost, Walhart's 49 Defense now goes to 53 Defense. Chill Def 3 and Threaten Atk 3 lower his enemies' Atk and Def so that Walhart can minimize damage as much as possible while being able to do as much damage as possible. If you feel Walhart is already getting enough damage against his foes from his normal attacks, you can replace Threaten Atk 3 with Savage Blow 3 or if you need Walhart in a Cavalry Emblem team, you can replace Threaten Atk 3 with Ward Cavalry, Hone Cavalry, Goad Cavalry, or Fortify Cavalry. As for his Assist, there is always the go-to Reposition for extended mobility. Or if you want him to be in-character, you can also change his Assist to Harsh Command. Now for his Special, his best Specials are Bonfire or Ignis, because they feed off his high Defense. You could also run Astra if you wish or can't afford Bonfire/ Ignis. --

builds.name: Lone Wolf
builds.desc: Like the name suggests, this build excels at dealing with large groups of physical enemies alone. Buff him up with various skills turn one and send him in to wreck havoc, or just solo an arena assault that has all physical units. He uses many skills well, so even if you're working on a budget, he should have the ability to lead the charge.

builds.name: Lone Conqueror
builds.desc: My personal be-all, end-all Walhart build. He slaughters just about everything he touches, and if he can't reasonably win a situation due to an abundance of mages, he can hurl someone else in with Smite or Shove - or use his Assist to push an ally away. Solo skills generally help Walhart's Wolf Berg reach peak damage capabilities, and if you have the Edelgard to spare, Rouse just makes it all the more powerful. I run this loadout with Atk/Spd, Vantage, and Threaten, and it's essentially carried me through most content. Close Foil can also be used in the A slot, but I personally wouldn't recommend it because it only counters colorless bows.

builds.name: Mjölnir Frontline
builds.desc: A variation of Lone Conqueror adapted for Mjölnir's Strike Shield phase. It maintains the same principle of emphasizing Wolf Berg's power in isolation, but exchanges a few skills to make defense easier. Speed is preferred here because in most cases, you're not going to be counterattacked, especially if you're prioritizing tomes that can take out other teammates, and Walhart's defense under extreme investment (high merges, max Dragonflowers) is going to be so stacked that most physical weapons will hardly damage him, if at all. Even so, Desperation makes for a good "just in case" measure, in the event that something manages to knock his health down. Heavy Blade makes Galeforce much easier to proc with his high attack, though you're not always guaranteed to outscore the enemy.

builds.name: Scourge of the Shepherds
builds.desc: Walhart is a very easy character to +10. This build is incredibly powerful, and can take out multiple teams with ease. If alone, it is rare he will take damage from physical attackers, but be cautious of magical attackers, as his Res leaves a lot to be desired.
